children: For Mugalli, the larger competitive risk comes from an established industry leader. "The real threat is Samsung," he said.
Mugalli pointed to Samsung’s confirmation in July that it is building substantial new fab capacity and said that it "has the balance sheet to chase market share."
"That’s the one I am watching," he said.
The distinction has become increasingly important as memory shares sell off on concerns about future supply.
Micron, SanDisk, SK Hynix and Samsung have all faced pressure in October as investors debate whether new capacity could eventually end the current period of tight memory supply.
